# `table3_records`

**Table III records**

One row per classification record on one act's OLRC Table III page: which U.S. Code place each section of a public law went to, as the page states it. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.

**Coverage.** Sampled. Measured on one cold-start run (receipt `d1-measured-run-2026-09-19/`), and the measurement is mostly a refusal: of the 108 acts the law route listed, 2 were read and produced 65 rows, 5 were refused, and the walk then stopped for the Congress with 99 acts unread — the per-run cap of 300 was never approached. One Table III page per public law the law route listed for the scoped Congresses, oldest first, under that cap; an act already published is not re-read. *(measured 2026-09-19)*

**Data quality.** Two things keep rows out of this table, and the measured run met the second far harder than the first. Table III lags enactment by tens of laws (the 119th stood at 119-73 there while the law route reached 119-110, measured 2026-09-14), and an act it does not yet hold answers a page cut off inside the site menu, which the reader refuses.
The second is the publisher's transport. On 2026-09-19 `uscode.house.gov` answered `GET /table3/{congress}_{n}.htm` with `200 OK` and its headers, then closed the connection partway through the chunked body: `httpx` raises `RemoteProtocolError: peer closed connection without sending complete message body (incomplete chunked read)`, which the acquirer reports as a transport failure after its three retries. It is intermittent per page, not per act — `119_1` and `119_4` were served whole in the same run while `119_2`, `119_3`, `119_5`, `119_6` and `119_7` were not — and it is invisible to a status-code check, because the status line is a clean `200`. It was re-derived outside the rollup with a plain `httpx.get` to confirm it is the publisher's and not the acquirer's.
The rollup's two guards did their job and bounded the damage: each refused act was stepped past and left to the next run, and three consecutive refusals ended that Congress's walk, so the run spent 25 OLRC requests rather than 300 and stopped with 99 of the 108 listed acts unread. Of the 2 acts that were read, 65 rows were published. A refused act holds nothing behind it and is retried next run, so the table fills as the publisher's body serving allows rather than failing the rollup.
An act's page is read once: a later edit to it (a status moving to repealed) is not picked up, and `release_point` says how current the captured page was. Private laws and pre-1957 session-law chapters are not requested. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.

- **Parquet file:** `table3_records.parquet`
- **Queryable via MCP `query_sql`:** Yes

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `act_key` | `VARCHAR` | The act key requested: a public law number, or a pre-1957 session-law chapter. |
| `stated_key` | `VARCHAR` | The act key as the page itself states it, en dash and all. |
| `seq` | `VARCHAR` | Zero-based position of this record on the page. |
| `congress` | `VARCHAR` | The Congress the page states for the act. |
| `act_date` | `VARCHAR` | The act's date as the page states it. |
| `statutes_at_large_volume` | `VARCHAR` | The volume the page states for the act. |
| `release_point` | `VARCHAR` | The currency the page states in its Table III Tool banner. |
| `act_section` | `VARCHAR` | The act section this record classifies. |
| `record_volume` | `VARCHAR` | The volume in this record's own statviewer link, where it carries one. |
| `record_page` | `VARCHAR` | The Statutes at Large page for this record. |
| `usc_title` | `VARCHAR` | The Code title the section went to; NULL where it went nowhere. |
| `usc_section` | `VARCHAR` | The Code section the section went to; NULL where it went nowhere. |
| `status` | `VARCHAR` | The page's status column for the record (repealed, omitted, and the like). |
| `observed_at` | `VARCHAR` | When the page was captured; the merge prefers the larger value. |
